# E137 -- Crafts Council

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Crafts Council
- **Industry:** Arts / Cultural Institution
- **Year:** c. 2007 (references to 2007 events and "end of 2007" renovation)
- **Source file:** c0b051d808842cbfacf828086ed66131.pdf
- **Scope:** Comprehensive brand guidelines covering brand strategy, tone of voice, visual toolkit, production, partnerships, and examples

## Brand Strategy
- **Role:** The national development agency for contemporary crafts in the UK
- **Core idea:** "Material Culture" -- not a strapline but the encapsulation of what the Crafts Council is about
- **Vision:** To position the UK as the best place in the world for making, seeing, and collecting contemporary craft
- **Positioning:** "The UK's first port of call for craft"
- **Offer areas:** Knowledge (expertise, information), Partnership (curatorial, educational, commercial), Advocacy (promotion, opinion)
- **Values (4):** Confident (knowledgeable, challenging, strategic), Enjoyable (fun, vibrant, welcoming), Vital (surprising, imaginative, flexible), Open-minded (transparent, inquisitive, collaborative)
- **Brand blueprint:** A succinct one-page framework linking vision, offer, idea, positioning, and values

## Logo
- **Form:** Circular mark -- described as "a perfect circle, but with a bit missing" (an incomplete/open circle form)
- **Minimum size:** 12mm from top to bottom
- **Exclusion zone:** One quarter of the overall height of the logo
- **Positioning:** Top left corner of page wherever possible
- **Color usage:** Black logo on backgrounds lighter than 50% tonal value; white logo on backgrounds darker than 50%
- **Sizing per format:** Specific logo sizes prescribed per standard format (A3: 48mm, A4: 36mm, standard 210x140: 24mm, A5: 24mm, A6: 20mm, business card: 20mm)
- **Background rules:** Can appear on textures, photographic images, and non-palette colors with tonal value rules

## Typography
- **Primary font:** Calvert MT -- a modern British slab serif typeface; used for headlines, sub-headings, body copy, and labels
- **Primary weights:** Light and Bold only (Regular excluded from identity despite being available)
- **Secondary font:** OCRB -- mono-spaced typeface; used for captions, credits, and legal copy; one weight (Medium)
- **System font:** Arial (Regular and Bold only) -- for email and online where Calvert/OCRB unavailable
- **Alignment:** All body copy, captions, and most titles ranged left, unjustified
- **Typographic conventions:** Bold for titles (never in body copy), superscript for dates, underscores for emphasis in body copy, rules for structural separation in listings
- **Hierarchy guidance:** Detailed advice on type size relationships, word spacing, interline spacing, kerning at larger sizes
- **Emphasis methods:** Color change, underscore, or weight change -- never combine methods

## Color
- **Palette size:** 9 colors
- **Key colors (with Pantone refs):**
  - Dark grey/blue -- PMS 7546 C / RGB 44, 51, 63
  - Dark brown -- PMS 497 C / RGB 62, 24, 21
  - Blue -- PMS 279 C / RGB 137, 175, 222
  - Orange -- PMS 163 U / RGB 216, 145, 63
  - Green -- PMS 7480 C / RGB 124, 185, 129
  - Olive/sage -- PMS 5783 C / RGB 177, 181, 136
  - Lime/chartreuse -- PMS 389 C / RGB 212, 226, 41
  - Mint/teal -- PMS 7464 C / RGB 198, 222, 213
  - Pale green -- PMS 7485 C / RGB 232, 236, 218
- **Comprehensive specs:** Each color specified in Pantone coated, Pantone uncoated, CMYK coated, CMYK uncoated, and RGB
- **Type color preference:** Dark brown preferred for text; black and grey as alternatives; never more than one text color at a time
- **Graphic device:** Can be used in any palette color

## Graphics
- **Graphic device:** Two overlapping circles -- one emanating from the logo position (top-left), one from the bottom-left corner of the page; circles scaled until they touch
- **Construction:** 4-step geometric construction method clearly documented; the device scales and adapts to different format orientations
- **Versions:** Solid fill and keyline (either can be used for any application)
- **Symbolism:** Represents the Crafts Council's connection with numerous craft disciplines and the influence/guidance they offer
- **Format adaptation:** Circle positions shift for landscape (center moves left ~1/5 of width) and portrait (center moves up ~2/5 of depth) formats

## Photography
- **Four categories:** Objects and backgrounds, Objects and places, Objects and people, Pictures of people
- **Quality standards:** Aesthetically pleasing and technically proficient; must reflect brand values
- **Objects and backgrounds:** Neutral surroundings that complement the object; careful consideration of background interaction with the craft object
- **Resolution minimums:** 72dpi on-screen at 100%, 300dpi in print at 100%
- **Style direction:** Images should be visually engaging and feature craft objects and people prominently

## Applications
- **Grid system:** Highly detailed modular grid -- baseline grid (1mm increments), 4-column grid with 8-column subdivision, image grid aligned to both
- **Standard format:** 140w x 210mm (Crafts Council standard); margins top 6mm / bottom 12mm / left 6mm / right 12mm
- **Production section:** Covers materials, finishing, and commitment to the environment
- **Partnerships section:** Addresses brand hierarchy when co-branding with partner organizations
- **Examples section:** Practical applications demonstrating the identity in use

## Tone of Voice
- **Foundation:** Derived from the four brand values (Confident, Enjoyable, Vital, Open-minded)
- **Six guiding principles:**
  1. Celebrate the subject -- be proud of ambition; talk about craft in a surprising, inquisitive, knowledgeable way
  2. Don't claim, explain -- give figures and quotes instead of vague claims; be transparent
  3. Think yourself into the reader's mind -- ask "who will read this?" and speak directly to them
  4. Expect intelligence but not expertise -- never dumb down, but always explain specialist language
  5. Use a confident, direct style -- avoid jargon; use active voice and first person plural; be direct and welcoming
  6. Always check against the brand blueprint -- assess which values to emphasize per audience
- **Golden rules:** Write and re-write, be clear and concise, avoid bad grammar, test-run work with colleagues, proofread everything
- **Extensive before/after examples** showing how to transform institutional language into engaging, specific communication

## Outliers
- **Unusually detailed typography chapter** -- covers word spacing, interline spacing, kerning, and alignment as standalone topics; more instructional than most brand guidelines
- **Geometric graphic device construction** -- the two-circle system is a distinctive and mathematically defined branding element
- **OCRB as secondary font** -- an unusual choice; a mono-spaced optical character recognition typeface used for captions/credits gives a technical, institutional-yet-contemporary feel
- **Production and environment section** -- rare for brand guidelines to cover material choices and environmental commitment
- **Before/after tone of voice examples** are exceptionally well-written and instructive, comparing generic institutional copy with specific, engaging alternatives

## Quality Score
**4 / 5** -- A thorough, well-structured guide that excels in its tone of voice section (among the best before/after examples seen) and its unusually detailed typography education. The grid system documentation is rigorous. The color palette is generous at 9 colors with full spec breakdowns. Loses a point for its age (c. 2007) and the fact that some visual sections (photography, graphic device) rely heavily on images that cannot be assessed via text extraction. The slab-serif + mono-spaced type pairing is distinctive and well-reasoned.
